messages:
Aisha: quick sync - we need a concise routing playbook: when latency steering suggests nearest region but residency/consent forbids it, what is the precedence?

Tom: short answer: legal/consent constraints must win. If an account mandates EU-only, requests must not be routed outside EU. Make it an explicit precedence rule, not heuristics.

Lena: agreed, but experience shows many customers want 'soft' residency. Can we express Strict / Soft / None? Soft should be "prefer but allow" with audit.

Diego: propose two-layer model: 1) config (customer policy) is canonical; 2) runtime scorer (latency/capacity). Config overrides scorer for strict policies.

Aisha: implementation idea: policy modes -> {strict, prefer, none}. Strict = allowlist. Prefer = apply penalty to non-preferred regions. None = score by latency+capacity.

Tom: fallback behavior needs clarity. If preferred region hits capacity SLO, allow fallback but emit audit and set sticky TTL on that session so we don't oscillate. Also record fallback_reason and metric.

Lena: suggest concrete TTL windows: transient fallback: 30s; sustained fallback: 5m; operator override must be explicit. Those are operator-friendly defaults.

Diego: operational visibility: add routing header on proxied requests: X-Redwood-Route-Decision: region=eu-west-1;reason=consent;fallback=true;ttl=300;fallback_id=abc123

ops-bot: rollout started for routing-service v2.3 feature flag: jurisdictional-steering (canary).

Aisha: pseudocode sketch we can put in RFC appendix:
if account.policy.residency == "strict": candidates = filter(regions, in(policy.allowed))
else if account.policy.residency == "prefer": score = latency + preference_penalty(nonpreferred)
else: score = latency + capacity_penalty
apply capacity checks and slot limits
if no candidates -> if account.allows_global_fallback: choose best global region and emit audit event else: return 451 (residency_required)

Tom: important: global_fallback must be opt-in for regulated tenants. Default for accounts created via sales/legal should be strict unless explicitly changed.

Lena: add admin-only override header for debugging: X-RW-Force-Region (admin-only, audit every use). UI label proposals: "Data residency: Strict / Prefer / No preference" with short help text.

Diego: safety checklist before rollout: 1) preserve KV-cache-affinity tags when redirecting so we don't trigger cache stampede and increased latency; 2) ensure session cookies/hints persist across fallback region so client sessions don't break; 3) canary with synthetic tenants that exercise prefer/strict modes.

Aisha: also recommend emitting these telemetry events: routing.choice, routing.fallback, routing.override, routing.audited_denied. Include fields: account_id, reason, chosen_region, latency_ms, capacity_headroom, fallback_ttl.

Tom: we should also model capacity headroom threshold for degradation: e.g., avoid sending to preferred region if headroom < 10% unless strict. That prevents SLO erosion.

Lena: UX question: when we show "preferred but routed elsewhere" in account history, include link to audit log and the fallback window expiration time.

Diego: note about multi-tenant hardware: for Dedicated customers with tenant pinning, residency policy must map to physical host pools, not just region label. Add mapping table in config schema.

Aisha: next steps: Tom+Diego draft RFC appendix with config schema (policy modes, allowed_regions[], fallback_grace_seconds, allow_global_fallback boolean), header contract, and telemetry schema. Lena will prepare UI copy. I'll schedule a 30m review tomorrow.

ops-bot: Canary flag enabled in staging. Metrics for preferred vs fallback latency will be available in ~10m.

Aisha: thanks all. We want the RFC appendix ready for review before EOD tomorrow.
